# UX rules

Every rule has an ID. A feature spec and the code cite the ID (`design system UX-1`); they do not copy the rule. Each rule names the guard test that proves it, or `none yet`.

<!-- rule-table:start -->
| ID | Rule | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| UX-1 | **Consistent.** The same thing looks and behaves the same everywhere. | none yet |
| UX-2 | **Reused components.** A part that nearly fits is extended, never copied. | none yet |
| UX-3 | **Clear.** One headline says where you are; plain words, never raw codes as the main text. | none yet |
| UX-4 | **One primary action per screen**, labelled by what it does. | none yet |
<!-- rule-table:end -->

These four are examples. Replace them with the project's own rules.
